assumptions: k-let-preserving shuffles of each map are the null for that map's own extremes.
The promoter, splice and repeat models are the ones named, at their published scoring.
limits: A rate against chance is not a manufacturability verdict; a vendor's limits are check_manufacturability's question.
Cost is about a third of a second per map per shuffle for the promoter scan.
bio.jane/contract.question: How often does a corpus of maps carry a cryptic promoter, splice site or synthesis-breaking repeat more extreme than chance?

description: Measure how often a corpus of maps carries a cryptic σ70 promoter, a cryptic splice site or a synthesis-breaking repeat MORE EXTREME THAN CHANCE, rather than how many it carries. Every map of a few kilobases spells promoters, splice donors and repeats, so a raw hit count measures length and composition; here each map's own extreme (its most negative promoter ΔG, its highest MaxEntScan donor and acceptor score, its longest homopolymer, tandem repeat, repeated stretch and hairpin arm) is scored against k-let-preserving shuffles of that same map, and the false discovery rate is controlled across the corpus within each statistic. No statistic uses a threshold: none of the three models publishes one, and a vendor's repeat limit is a product's capability, which `check_manufacturability` answers instead. The result is a per-statistic rate with an exact binomial interval, plus every map's own test. Cost is dominated by the σ70 scan at roughly a third of a second per map per shuffle, so a corpus of maps at the default 99 shuffles is minutes of work; drop `flags` to the statistics you need to make it cheaper.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: false discovery rate at which a record counts towards a flag's rate.

correction.description: Benjamini–Hochberg (independent or positively dependent tests) or Benjamini–Yekutieli (any dependence; less power). Values: BH (Benjamini–Hochberg), BY (Benjamini–Yekutieli).

flags.description: which statistics to run. Empty runs all seven.

include_subject.description: also test the node's subject (the open or wired record).

seed.description: seed for the shuffles. Each record draws from seed + its own index, so a record's answer does not depend on the rest of the corpus. Advanced.

sequences.description: the corpus: wire upstream records here, or list library document names. Each is one record of the sweep.

shuffle_k.description: k-let size the shuffles preserve. 2 holds every dinucleotide count, which is what all three statistics read.

shuffles.description: shuffles per record. The smallest p the null can give is 1 / (shuffles + 1), which is what bounds how small a corrected q can get.

name: discover_flag_rates

hitCount.description: how many (record, statistic) tests were called

hits.description: every record whose statistic beat chance, smallest p first

nullModel.description: the null the p-values stand on, stated with every run

rates.description: per statistic: records tested, records above chance, the rate and its exact 95% interval

sweep.description: the full result, including the records tested

tests.description: every (record, statistic) test: the observed statistic, the shuffles' mean, p, q and the Monte Carlo interval
